item.title: Tremor recorded as Israel says Hezbollah tunnels destroyed in south Lebanon
item.description:
Israel said Thursday it demolished key tunnels built by the Iran-backed Hezbollah group beneath the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon, with a 4.1 magnitude tremor recorded in the area.

"This is strategic terrorist infrastructure that was built over two decades, with Iranian funding and planning," said a joint statement by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz.

The destruction "completes the achievement of operational control over the Ali al-Taher ridge -- above and below ground", the statement added.

item.title: Morocco says not involved in Ceuta migrant influx
item.description:
Morocco said on Thursday there were "no facts" establishing its involvement in the massive migrant rush into Spain's North African exclave of Ceuta in July.

More than 70,000 migrants entered Ceuta from Morocco on July 30 and 31 in an unprecedented, chaotic surge that left scores dead and sparked European Union infighting over the touchy issue of migration.

The Moroccan foreign ministry said there were "no facts or reports proving any involvement by the Moroccan authorities".

item.title: Israel says it destroyed Hezbollah tunnels in Ali al-Taher ridge: What to know
item.description: The ridge has become a flashpoint in the Israel-Hezbollah conflict in Lebanon due to its extensive tunnel network Israel says is utilized by the Iran-backed group.

item.title: Israeli-made film about Gaza gets 25-minute ovation at Venice premiere
item.description:
A chilling new documentary about Israel's AI-powered mass killing of civilians in Gaza from two Oscar-winning Israeli filmmakers received a 25-minute ovation at its premiere at the Venice Film Festival on Thursday.

The audience clapped continuously for Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor after the screening, an AFP reporter witnessed, setting what is thought to be a new record in Venice after a 23-minute ovation for another film about Gaza last year.

item.title: Likely oil slicks in Strait of Hormuz after US tanker strikes: experts
item.description:
Recent satellite images analysed on Thursday appear to show oil slicks near the Strait of Hormuz, after US strikes on tankers suspected of links to Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

An image from the European Copernicus programme taken on Wednesday shows brownish streaks on the surface of the water some 20 kilometres (nearly 12.5 miles) off the Iranian coast, to the east of the strait.

Another Copernicus image of the same location taken on Thursday shows winding streaks of a similar length.

item.title: UAE to invest 40 billion euros in Germany, including for data centres: Berlin
item.description:
The leader of the United Arab Emirates was on a state visit to Germany on Thursday that resulted in a promise to invest 40 billion euros ($46.5 billion) into Europe's top economy.

The money would partly pay for data centres with a capacity of up to one gigawatt, Berlin said, and an "Investment Council" would be set up to boost business links between the two nations.

The Gulf is a key source of capital for the AI boom as oil-rich states in the region seek to invest their energy wealth.
